For getting started, you can get the KIs and cells/periapts from Voidwatch Officers (for cruor for the latter). Atmacite NPC can teleport for 1k cruor, but it just set everyone at the zoneline to Southern San d'Oria in East Ronfaure.

Where does this start?
There's dialogue in Pashow_S but it doesn't appear to be necessary. Just find a Voidwatch Officier and get a voidstone & stratum abyssite.

Just fought a Puk called Sarimanok in East Ronfaure. Me: NIN/WAR  alt: WHM/BLM

THF mob, incredibly high evasion and decent triple attack rate. Triple attack rate seems to increase as HP goes down. First 50% it only used Wind Shear/Crosswind for TP moves, and Aeroga2 and Aero4 for spells.

After 50% it started to get a little crazy. Started using Ill Wind (~700-800 AoE). Used Somnial Durance (AoE sleep), followed by instant-cast Aeroga3 for ~1k with shell5 up. This combo also caused a full hate reset. At this point it went after my WHM alt and killed her, followed by me shortly after.

Seems doable by 2 people if  well prepared (I was not), 3-4 people shouldn't have too much of a problem.

Unless he starts doing something even nastier after 25%, which is entirely possible.

Parsed about 40% acc against him (no sushi), Blade: Hi hit for 600-1500

Cells are 3k AN each under stars;  you can buy all of them from the npc.

Just did Sallow Seymour in North Gustaberg and also got Periapt of Exploration.

We didn't appear to get any white triggers or white enhancing items but got the periapt anyway.  We proc'd a few times, treasure was trash NPC shit.

One thing of note though: We brought a guy with no voidstone with us to test if he'd get KI drop (he used his earlier).  He did not.

The periapt of exploration seemed to cut the remaining time towards my next voidstone by 250 minutes or so.  That seems close to 20% (240 minutes), same as abyssite of celerity for traverser stones.

Also, it does not matter if you are dead if the NM dies, EXP/Cruor and key items will drop to you when you examine the chest after killing the NM.

Voidwatcher status lasts for three minutes after the NM's defeat to aloow raises and collection of loot.

That's about it for now.  Would recommend anyone planning on doing Voidwatch to hit up the worm ASAP.

If you don't want to waste potential limit points, stay in limit mode while doing Voidwatch.  Seems many of these NMs get new abilities and start to spam once they start getting below 25ish%.

If you're going for white stagger, and most people would if you want periapt/atmacite, you'll need to stagger highly vulnerable. It seems of the random vulnerabilities that the NM has, there will always only be 2 that are highly vulnerable, and those never change until procced. They're only expended if you open a winning chest, pretty much... so if you're low-man and everyone has time, if your initial 2 highly vulnerable procs are not favorable to you, run out / depop the NM and try again - the staggers will be different. Especially useful if you want white.

Couple of confirming questions for people well-seasoned on the event:

1) There were a couple of random testimonials that you can proc mobs even during their TP/spells.  Is this the general consensus (like Dynamis stuff)?

2) With respect to vulnerable/highly vulnerable weaknesses, once you get the message, is it the case that ANY action in that category can proc the mob?  For example, if you get "X is highly vulnerable to Great Sword weapon skills," I know from reading the thread that the highly vulnerable weakness will not CHANGE till procced.  But I just want to confirm that it can be pretty much any GS skill (like Dynamis too).

1) you can proc anytime

2) Not all, only ONE specific abi/ja/spell from the category it hints you will proc. However if you get both highly vulnerable and vulnerable WS/JA/spell, that means there is 2 moves from that category that will proc. eg. Highly vulnerable and vulnerable to greatsword weakness means 1 WS will proc w/o white light, and the other will proc white light. This also apply if you get 2 vulnerable or 2 highly vulnerable ja/ws/spell, except you can only be able to tell if you proced once, and the same message appear again(must make sure u proc in that category and it appear again). example highly vulnerable GS and you proc with hard slash, next weakness hints you again with highly vulnerable GS and then you can cycle all the other WS again and 1 of them will proc yet again.

Yeah you can proc at any time..

At any given moment the NM has 2 highly vulnerable weakness and like 4-6 vulnerable weaknesses.

The highly vulnerable ones never change until procced, and will give you white lights. The vulnerable ones, I think they cycle around a set pool of skills, or the actual number is very big - these seem to change.

ws procs will grant you blue lights ( for drop quantity) and magic procs give red lights ( for drop quality, tho i think this is a bit of BS and works more like drop rate because I've gotten unique weapon drop with base 100% ). I think abilities proc blue too, afaict. if you proc these on highly vulnerable you gain a lot more on colors too. Yellow and green comes with everything. White, when procced by highly vulnerable always increases by 25%.

so if u want atma/periapt you need 4 highly vulnerable procs to guarantee a drop.

edit2 : im pretty sure non-high procs can also give white, but not always.

The 2 highly vulnerable procs seem to be picked at random, and if you don't have anyone who can trigger those 2, then you're basically screwed on white / high procs for that battle. It can be 2 ws, 2 magic, or ws and ja, or 1 of each.. no set pattern.

Also, when theres vulnerability, its 1 specific ws or spell they're looking for, so if you have used something, move on to another spell/ws. i'm pretty sure trial/relic/mythic/empyrean ws are included in this list too.. so be prepared for them..

and finally, if you get both nq and highly vulnerable hints for the same ws/spell type, that simply means there are 2 procs from there.

A small note on Hahava about Raksha/Yaksha Stance.

Raksha Stance is only MDT-50% while Yakska is PDT-50% (ranged attacks included), it seem to switch between the two about every 2~ min or so.

It can use the following TP moves after Raksha Stance (which dispel 3 buffs and gives it MDT-50%) :

Raksha: Judgment (AoE magical damage, amnesia/bind/silence, 600~800 dmg)

Raksha: Illusion (cone attack magical damage, para/curse -50% hp/mp, 800~1200 dmg and hits from VERY far away)

Under 50%(?)

Raksha: Vengeance (AoE magical damage, 1 min weakness/muddle, 800~1200 dmg, can be stunned)

After Yashka Stance (PDT-50%) :

Yaksha: Damnation (cone attack physical damage, 400~600 dmg)

Yaksha: Bliss (cone attack physical damage, ATK/MAB down, 200~500 dmg)

Under 50%

Yaksha: Oblivion (AoE physical damage, all stats down -110, 1300~2200 dmg, can be stunned too but the window is much shorter)

He has already the Yashka Stance effect at the start (at least for us, maybe it's random).

You only need to pay attention for Raksha: Vengeance after Raksha Stance. I'm pretty sure this move is used under 50% like Yaksha: Oblivion.

When you know all of this it becomes even more a joke. Smn can switch between Predator Claw and Merit BP depending on the "Stance".

1) Click the "Edit" button at the top of the page. We use Templates to make life easier, so you (sometimes) end up with gibberish unless you click the top.

2) * = bullet point.

3) ** = sub-bulletpoint.

4) [[Something]] = Link to a page on wiki named Something.

5) [http://url Words Words (Name, Website)] = External link to http://url with the text "Words words (Name, Website)" which is the format I've been using for citations.

There are no silence or amnesia staggers, and there are no blue !! staggers in Voidwatch.

The staggers that I've seen are:

Normal Vulnerability:

Lower: Grellow !! (Adds 20% light to main affected light, restores 1 temp item if you have temp KIs)

Higher: Red !! (Adds 40% light to main affected light, restores all temp items if you have temp KIs)

High Vulnerability:

Lower: Red !! (Adds 100% light to main affected light, restores all temp items if you have temp KIs)

Higher: Red !! (Adds 200% light to main affected light, restores all temp items if you have temp KIs)

The lights added by a stagger depend on what caused the stagger. A magical stagger will add red light as the main affected light, while a JA or WS stagger will add blue light as the main affected light. Spectral alignments colors have no correlation with !! colors.

So any high stagger is red !!, and low stagger is red !! maybe 1/3 of the time (seems to be a bias towards the lower stagger in each group). All staggers are terror. Grellow lasts about 5 seconds (long enough to throw a WS on the Blitz if you're already engaged, but not really long enough to engage, run in, and WS if you're standing back), red lasts much longer (15-30, I haven't timed and I don't know if it varies).

Just confirmation on how TH works, figured it out in tonight's run. Some of this stuff was previously posted, but I just wanted to repost as confirmation on where the TH comes into the formula for the final alignments. TH effect is 1% per TH level, up to 6% maximum. The percentage multiplies the total alignment including ascent items, but NOT including periapts.

((Base + Staggers) + Ascent) * Treasure Hunter + Periapt = Total

Max of Base + Staggers is 350 for red/blue, 225 for green/yellow

Max of ((Base+Staggers) + Ascent) * Treasure Hunter is assumedly 500% for all because blue and red cannot be increased further by Treasure Hunter if they are already capped at 500%, while green and yellow can since they cap at 300% with max staggers/ascent items.

Periapts seem to be the only thing that can increase alignment beyond 500%.

So, for example, if blue was 300% at the end of the fight and you receive 6% treasure hunter, have the periapt for blue light, and used three cells, your blue light would end up being (300+150)*1.06 + 25 = 502%.

One confirmation of this that I didn't try myself would be to cap red or blue with staggers but without using ascent items (350%) and see if Treasure Hunter adds light. If it does, then the above should be correct. If not, may need a little tweaking.

Spoiler: showDo we have any means yet of measuring what exactly red% does for the loot pool other than the assumption it increases the NM drops?

Blue is easy to determine since it's 100% for each slot to roll on in the chest (cells + KI + max blue = 525%, which gives 5 slots with a 1/4 chance on a 6th slot also), but I'm not seeing any means of measuring what exactly red does.

Red could perhaps work the same way?  Each 100% could = a roll for each slot granted by blue to be a roll for one of the worthwhile items.  The treasure pool list would be assumed to be sorted though for that to make any sense, since the drops always appear at the top.

One of the only two bodies my LS got (after many, many T4s) was to someone who didn't even trade cells. Also, someone in my LS has gotten both Voidwrought Plate and Strendu Ring off of the same Voidwrought, so it's at least possible for the material and one of the armor pieces to drop.

I would assume red just impacts the mob-specific item drop rate directly. For example, if the drop rate of Fazheluo R.Mail is normally 0.1% at 100% red, it would be 0.5% at 500% red. As far as the loot system goes, I don't really expect them to change it. Meanwhile, if you have a bunch of people who know what they're doing and know how to get around Vana'diel quickly, this is certainly one of the slicker events in the game in terms of keeping things moving and minimizing inactive time (city earrings and retrace staves are brilliant for this; for example, Federation Earring drops you about 50 steps south of the Voidwatch NPCs in Windurst Waters). Everything else seems to drop with a fairly reasonable rate, and there are those odd fights where you get some quantity of drops that blows any other NM from any other event out of the water (e.g. one Moira we did last night dropped three crowns, three bomblets, and a molar - this type of loot pool would be impossible with normal distribution).

I am almost certain that what Arthars posted earlier in this thread (or in the Weakness thread, I don't remember which) is true. He suggested that the higher staggers (40% normal, 200% high) happen during or just after a mob TP move. Initially, I was pretty sure it wasn't the case, because we actually stunned a couple of TP moves on Voidwrought with weaknesses which only led to low staggers (20%), but I think Voidwrought was just a fluke (Ironclads are dumb like that). Last night on Celaeno, we were timing our procs and every one that was landed on a spell or TP move resulted in a higher stagger (again, 40% or 200%, vs. 20% or 100%), and this was the case on several runs in the past as well, though we weren't specifically trying to time our staggers prior to last night. Can anyone else confirm (or deny) this?

Couple things:

1 - Blitz almost definitely has no cap. We got an amazing series of staggers the other night that kept Celaeno frozen from ~80% to below 20% HP and the blitz result was over a 150% increase in alignments.

2 - Confirming that Treasure Hunter calculation is based on the sum of alignment from cells and weakness staggers with the cap at 500% before the effect of any alignment-enhancing periapts. Got 506% alignment with capped blue trading two cells, 7% TH ( (350+100)*1.07 + 25).

Also, further confirmation that proc-ing a stagger while a mob is casting or using a TP move results in the higher alignment bonus for that tier of stagger (40% NQ, 200% HQ). This was a key find, credit to Arthars (note that Voidwrought is still all sorts of fucked up and this doesn't work every time on him, in addition to TH being broken on him).

Just noticed on your Voidwatch guide for the nations path, you mention blue !! showing up for JA/WS weakness. There are no blue !! in voidwatch, the color of the !! doesn't correspond to the color of the lights increased. Red !! is for any high stagger, grellow !! is only for the lowest one. Normal weakness stagger can still yield red !! if it was hit while the mob was casting a spell or readying a TP move. Four kinds of staggers are...

Normal vulnerability stagger: 20 R or B / 10G / 10Y / 0W (grellow !!, 1 used temp item returned, 5 sec stagger)

Normal vulnerability stagger timed on a mob's TP move or spell cast: 40 R or B / 50G / 50Y / 25W (red !!, all used temp items returned, ~20 sec stagger)

High vulnerability stagger: 100 R or B / 50G / 50Y / 25W (red !!, all used temp items returned, ~20 sec stagger)

High vulnerability stagger timed on a mob's TP move or spell cast: 200 R or B / 50G / 50Y / 25W (red !!, all used temp items returned, ~20 sec stagger)

The main light received (red or blue) depends on whether it was magic (red) or JA/WS (blue) that proc'ed - you have that part captured correctly.

First kill we had about 10 minutes left, second kill we had about 2 minutes left. Timed out once due to inability to proc weakness efficiently (had him invincible for over 7 minutes straight on that attempt). He certainly builds resistance to stun, like any other higher tier Voidwalkers mob. I think the most effective method of killing him is to sit on procs that you know you can hit and make sure you have a way to get those procs hit. For example, if you get a specific weapon message that you know you can hit a WS proc for, make sure you have enough TP wings/regain to get that proc off. I'd certainly sit on any easy JA procs that you get messages for. This way you can get that shield off right away. The shield can happen even over 50%, but it's rarer then. Shah Mat is not magical shield, it's just a temporary doom/terror gaze. Likewise, Bishop's Gambit itself is not physical shield - it just cures him for like 2200 and removes his debuffs. However, he occasionally puts up a shield right after gambit which makes him totally invulnerable to damage (below 50%, and certainly below 25%, the shield comes up almost every time).

As far as stunning goes, make sure your dark magic is capped at 95 (it does make a difference, I think it's like a 35 skill spread from 90 to 95?), and make sure your stunners are wearing full accuracy gear, Jupiter's Staff, (magians accuracy staff if you're crazy like that), etc. Need a good dark magic/accuracy set, not just whatever random gear you were wearing, and yeah definitely keep up Ascetic's Tonic if you can. I was on SCH last night, and I had little problem stunning, even after other people started to build resist (use Alacrity/Klimaform with Thunderstorm if you start running into major accuracy problems). Random jobs with BLM sub (WHM, even RDM) will definitely run into problems stunning rather quickly, though. All that being said, you will definitely have a few stuns resisted, and he'll certainly get the shield up at least a couple of times per fight. Just make sure you have known weaknesses ready to proc when that shield does go up. Frankly, if you know you have a weakness proc that you're sitting on, I think you're better off just letting him get the shield up sometimes and save the stun for Kaustra, since that almost always kills everyone it hits from the DoT if not from the initial damage.

Byakko has blind aura and the usual high evasion as a thf mob.  We used Stalwart's drink to deal with that.  Suzaku has paralyze and en-amnesia, plus his wind does high damage and silence like the Rocs in dynamis-Qufim.   Genbu is Genbu, and has high defense.  I'm not sure what his aura is. Rule #1 of wamouras: do not enfeeble the fucking wamouras. Try enfeeble procs and BLU spells with add effects last and only if you really need that proc.

Twilight Scythe seems to have it's own damage type, shared by nothing else players can get in the game.

On one hand, it ignores individual immunities or resistances to physical, magical, blunt, slashing, piercing, and spiritual type damage.

On the other hand, if a mob is coded to have resistance or immunities to all types of damage as a set, Twilight Scythe will do reduced/no damage (such as Excavation duty rocks, or Campaign mobs when they're warping away).  Twilght Scythe is also hampered if a mob is designed to be immune to all but one damage type, as well.

These also apply to mobs absorbing damage; a mob like Rani, which only absorbs a single type of damage at a time, will never absorb Twilight Scythe hits.  However, a mob like Shinryu with its wings out, will absorb Twilight Scythe hits because it's programmed to absorb everything.

For anyone wondering, it was mentioned above, but don't kill Qilin's adds. They have too much HP and it's a total waste of time. Qilin himself isn't very hard to hold, but if you stop killing him to kill the adds when they pop, he will definitely have regenned to 100%. Between the auras and their TP moves, the adds are actually more annoying to kill (and more deadly to a larger group) than Qilin. It's much easier to have a PLD (preferably one with Ochain or Aegis) standing off to the side and grabbing the adds as they pop, with a WHM dedicated to keeping them alive. This way everyone can focus on Qilin (controlled zerg capping lights along the way, make sure everyone has all temp items). Without anyone 2-hring and capping lights along the way, it dies in ~5 minutes with a full well-equipped alliance. If he gets lucky, he might kill one or two people. The fight went from "wtf how are we going to do this" to "this is probably the easiest T3" when we we switched our strategies from killing adds to pulling them away and focusing on Qilin. He'll typically be dead before he can get the third summon off if you use this method. Parses are a flawed base for evidence. Uncontrollable variables that will play on the accuracy of a test. Cold hard numbers and actual data and comparisons that make sense are the only truly accurate methods to gauge effectiveness in this and most any circumstance unless judging efficiency based on certain monsters or notorious monsters, person versus person, person vs specific monster or notorious monster, etc., or for gauging the effectiveness of factors such as Double Attack or Triple Attack over long periods of time as they are hardly acted upon by outside variables.

You can definitely trust Ejin's result as I have seen him in action. As for trying to find out how he averages so high, I have a few thoughts.

1) Looking at the parse, it seems like they have a Drg, at least for that fight, and for short fight like this, Angon can be really helpful for the duration of the fight as attack is generally the base of your WS damage.

3) Use your wing. If you are consistently procing, you should be getting wing all the time, and the difference between a 100% tp ukko and a 300% tp one is huge. 4) Eat food.

5) Don't forget accuracy on your WS. Most ppl, especially your pickup DD, think they are capped on accuracy since they are lvl 99. In Ig-Alima and Rex that's the worst thing you can assume. I see ppl blindly using Heafoc mitt on multi hit WS, stacking STR with no regard of accuracy. Stw. drink helps a bit, brave drink helps a bit, but not to a degree that you should completely forget accuracy.

Since some people are struggling to do the DD method, there's another way to beat it (I didn't watch the BLM video that was posted, so may be the same strategy, either way this saves them looking).

Have 3BLM together in a party with a COR, WHM, and a proc job of your choice. Those 3BLM and the COR are your main source of damage. The second party has a PLD and enough support for him so he can hold it without any danger of dying, and fill up free spots with procs of your choice. The last party has a WAR, a RNG/MNK, a healer or 2, and procs of your choice.

Take it slow till about 85% HP, to find out what procs are and so on. Save an obvious HV weakness(such as BRD songs/Abilities) and proc it at 85~80% HP. Have your BLM go all out while others keep trying to proc. When it unstaggers, it will always use a TP move and not Chainspell immediately. Stun once, use Fools, and zerg again till CS is off. Have your BLM use Douse, and take it slow till 30~35% again. Repeat the HV weakness process of earlier again and it's dead. Takes 6~7min, it's pretty safe if you don't have the DD/buffers to kill it that way.

A specific adjustment we have planned is to set blue and red alignment at their maximum values at the beginning of the battle.

Weakness revamps

Also, in regards to cases where the weakness is difficult or due to your setup you cannot exploit it even though you determined what it is, we are planning to perform appropriate adjustments. 1) My BLM gear kinda sucks, but Ascetic's/Braver's is very useful for this fight.

2) If you aren't in melee AoE range, use Fools as your last temp item during the initial spawning temp item spam. If you proc 0 times before he Chainspells, you're fucked anyway. You will trigger Chainspell before it wears, or you're fucked anyway. This guarantees your support won't be hurt by Chainspell and there will be fewer targets to heal.

3) Spam proc/damage spells on BLM, but when you get near 80% have one of the BLMs hold off for Stun and Stun after the first quick-casted spell (which actually occurs before chainspell in my log). This will give your DDs time to get Fools up.

4) Spam proc/damage spells during Chainspell (he takes extra damage? idr, maybe set procs), but towards the end you will want to hold off and ready Stun again. Stunning the first post-chainspell TP move will save most of your DDs and give them a chance to put up Fanatic's.

Hello guys,

I wanted to share my strat and experience with Botulus Rex-

After reading and attempting all the different strategies for Rex, I decided to try it this way

and realized it's more consistent/easier to find people compared to WAR zerg or WF spam.

The setup was:

PT1: BLM BLM BLM BLM WHM COR (WF)

PT2: BLM BLM BLM BLM WHM COR (WF)

PT3: WAR DRK RNG(WF) NIN BRD RDM

Make sure all the blms have thundaja and thunder5, also the corsair must have WF (only need 2 cor though compared to 4-6 CORs of the other strats)

and WF for RNG isnt mandatory, RNG is there mainly for procs.

Key members for this strat are WAR DRK RNG NIN (the proccers), they must have all weapons, temp items and most importantly, know how to play-

1. You have the WHMs drop pt and BRD does troubadour Scherzo in both BLM parties.

2. one COR will do tactician's roll in proccers' PT and warlock ROLL in one BLM pt, the other COR will do warlock/wizard.

3. set 2 BLMs to stun chainspell animation (@ 80% they gotta stop casting spells and focus on that) and

other 2 BLMs to stun 1st WS after chainspell's over.

4. Have one of the proccers pop it, use fanatic's while everyonelse uses their temp items + Parsimony + Elemental seal, make sure fanatic's

is the LAST temp item everyonelse uses.

5. Make sure everyone is spread around in circle around the rift, and not packed togheter.

6. Nuke it like crazy + COR spam WF, proc PT must focus on procs only, assign one BLM to BLM procs, and skip BLM1 procs.

7. Once it chainspells, 2 BLMs should stun by animation with a /p macro giving notice, everyone applies fool's drinks and keeps nuking.

8. By the time fool's wears (that should be around 2:30 into the fight, 30 while u pop temp items + 1min fanatic + 1min fools)

you should get one HQ proc, having all temp items recharged.

9. Finish it and enjoy your Jacaranda logs-

Pros: BLM have high survaivability compared to WARs thx to Manawall, stun and the fact that with 8 BLMs nuking the mob it will roam around.

Fight shouldnt last over 3-4 mins MAX, BLM deals a lot of DMG to it and technically u can even hold the mob by just stunning and kiting around

waiting for an HQ proc to land.

Cons: You need highly skilled proccers with most weapons (i.e. RNG with axe dagger, WAR with polearm scythe etc) and once u found out which proc it is make sure DDs communicate and split the WSs like (war does low scythe's WS and DRK does high ones)

So yeah compared to other strats I found this one easier to realize especially b/c it's easier to find decent BLMs compared to decent WF corsairs.

You are making Rex seem worse than it is manaburned. Have one PLD with enough support, fill the rest of that party with procs up. Have one party completely for procs(obviously with support so they don't die instantly), and the last party with BLMx4 COR WHM. One of the "procs" can be another BLM as well.

The most important thing with this would be to start it slowly. Try to find out as many procs as possible, and save the "easy" HVs such as bash/bard songs/etc. Time those HVs so that you hit one around 80-90%. At that point have your BLM go all out. DD keep trying to proc, without buffs they won't really matter for damage compared to the BLM and are a greater use if they hit another proc or two. If Rex is not below at least 70% after the stagger wears off, this strategy will not work without SMNs and your BLMs suck/you forgot the COR/drinks. If it is below 70%, he will use a TP move every time right after unstagger. This is where one of you stuns, and everyone should be using Fool's immediately. Again, during CS have your BLM go all out.

Enmity Douse after and repeat the same thing but save your HV for 40-30% this time. Works almost every time, only time it doesn't is when you get HV procs you didn't bring obviously.

We wiped to the colibri over and over the other night in a pug group but in the end we sussed it all out and had a VERY easy win on the final fight once we figured out the deal with its adds.

The colibri will pop a single add every time it uses Snatch Morsel whether it eats someones food or not. Once it pops a total of five or six adds it wont pop any more than that. Each add has a different elemental affinity and the pops seem to progress somewhat through the elemental wheel even though there are ultimately only 5 or 6 adds that will pop. The groups who are just having 2 pops are probably in a solid VW group that isn't a typical PUG run and prob are keeping the boss procced most of the fight, getting lucky w/ the TP moves the boss uses, and having VERY short fights. For a standard VW group/PUG the best way we found to deal with the colibri was to have the PLD tank the boss off to one side, feed it some TP and control the add pops. When the adds pop zerg them and kill them, once you have all 5 or 6 killed simply proc the boss like normal and kill it. Be mindful to watch out for the AOE charm move, if the entire group gets hit with charm the boss will go white and depop.

Super easy fight overall once you address the mechanics properly.

Strategic Notes:

Promathia Route T1

Lufaise Meadows: Abunnunu (Demon) + Gloam Servitor (WAR) and Gloam Servitor (BLM) (Demons)

This fight is not hard at all.  The WAR pet will sync up TP moves with the main NM, and the BLM pet will cast when the main NM decides to cast (apparently).  Either way, you can either zerg the BLM pet, or just have a PLD hold both of them.  Uses Accurst Spear which is AoE damage and curse and Hellborn Yawp which is AoE damage and (knockback?).  Also uses condemnation (damage + decent duration stun) and possibly other demon TP moves.  All NMs have fairly high attack/base damage, but as long as you have fanatics up you won't be taking much damage.

Suggested Strategy:  Nothing special.  Just hold pets, or have DD kill mage pet, and then destroy the main NM.  It's probably just easier to hold the pets.  You really only need one PLD.

Misareaux Coast: Tsui-Goab (Albino Mantis) + Bloodswiller Fly x 2

This is similar to any other mantis fight.  It's absolutely essential to hold the flies far away from the main NM.  It will use its unique TP move (Exorender) which will kill any fly pets that it hits.  If a fly dies at any point, Tsui-Goab will level up.  Other than that, this is a standard mantis fight.  Proc + kill.

Strategy: Hold pets at a considerable distance from NM with a PLD.  Other than that, treat like a higher-level Kaggen that doesn't use Death Prophet.  Dispel preying posture.

Uleguerand Range: Isarukitsck + Little Wingman (x3)

Poison potions are a good idea on this NM, but they're not compulsory.  The main issue here is the unique move Whiteout which is AoE Zombie, Sleep, and Damage.  It also uses Yawn (Gaze sleep), Frigid shuffle (Paralyze), and Beak Lunge.  It may also use Wing Whirl and Wing Slap, but I'm not sure.  The pets can definitely use these.  The pets have awkward enmity mechanics and may sync up TP moves, you can try to hold them, but it's really not worth it. NM also casts, but it's not horrible.

Strategy Just treat this like any other VW fight with pets.  Try to hold the pets, keep fanatics up.  Poison potions will speed things up, because you'll spend less time sleeping.  If it stays staggered, like any other VW fight, it can't hurt you, so proc like it's hot.

Attowha Chasm: Fjalar + Bloody Skull (up to 3)

This is the hardest.  He likes to do everything he can to prolong the fight.  He spawns Bloody Skulls after Hellsnap (AoE Stun) and they cast spells including gaIII and Sleepga.  This is problematic.  Fjalar also likes to AoE Terror/Damage (Thundris Shriek).  His unique moves are Dunur Strike (low AoE Damage) and Bilfrost Squall (high AoE Damage).   Cackle inflicts several status effects, most importantly Magic Defense Down.  It MUST be removed.

Strategy:  PLD is not required for this NM.  Although there may be working strategies with a PLD on the main NM and DDs killing skulls.  I had success as follows:

1.) Ride fools drink, not fanatics drink.  Scherzo helps with your ability to do this.

2.) Weaken the NM and buff up as much as possible.  Ageha + Dia II(I) + Chaos Roll and damage will go much faster.  Only use Bio II+ if it's necessary.

3.) Form a clerics drink order to remove Cackle.  TP moves will destroy you with MDEF down up, but won't kill you otherwise for the most part.

4.) Ignore the adds completely, except maybe to TP on after Thundris Shriek (which imparts an intimidation effect).

5.) Just like any other VWNM, if it stays proc'd, it can't hurt you.  There's obviously a bit of a luck element in that!

Aht Urghan Route T1

Mount Zhayolm: Vanasarvik + Elder's Imps (up to 5)

This NM is very weak.  It summons adds after Bugle Call, and uses Grating Tantara + Stifling Tantara (Aoe Damage + amnesia / silence, respectively).  But these are blocked by fanatic's.  Adds sync TP moves, and it's best to hold them if they pop.  Really though?  Just keep it terror locked and it will never summon them.

Strategy: Hold adds, ride fanatics, and treat like any other VW fight.

Arrapago Reef: Dimgruzub + Assassan's Apprentice (x2)

While he can do some AoE attack that can wipe the floor with some mages, for the most part, this fight is extremely easy.  Have a PLD hold the pets (Ochain), and the rest of the alliance can gently touch themselves while they kill the main NM.  It takes 10x normal damage, but has 5 million HP or so; it's ridiculous.  Enjoy.  Make light skillchains for extra lulz.

Strategy: Hold adds, ride fanatics, and treat like any other VW fight.  Try not to drool on your keyboard.

Caedarva Mire Brekekekex + Chorus Toad (up to 8)

This fight is just like any other Poroggo NM including that he can use Frog Chorus (Charmga).  He also can use Chainspell at low HP.  The adds can be held, and have ensilence.  They'll eventually become a problem for mages, but even that's not an issue if they have fanatics.  I think it's better just to hold them and kill the main NM.  You can't dispel Frog Cheer.

Strategy: Hold adds, and ride fanatics, proc and zerg.  At low HP, he'll use chainspell.  use fools immediately and try to zerg him before chainspell ends, and he'll likely never use Frog Chorus that way.  He's very squishy.  Mages should use fanatics if they're being bothered, or if melees get charmed.

Mamook: Yalungur + Predatory Colibri (Up to 6)

The adds on this fight can cause a problem.  Each casts a single spell (Thundaja, Firaja, Comet, Holy, etc.) and they are spawned after using Snatch Morsel.  If it steals your food, it levels up, so DO NOT USE FOOD.  It's a bard, and will cast songs like Mambo etc., but doesn't seem to use Virelai.  At low HP, it can use WISECRACK (Aoe Charm).  If the entire group is charmed, it will depop.  Tropic Tenor is its unique move, which is AoE damage + all stats down.  It uses this a lot.

Strategy:  It's best to kill the adds.  They can wreak havoc.  It won't pop more than 6 of them.  Just have a PLD tank the NM and pull the adds off and zerg them.  Other than that, it's a straightforward proc+zerg fight with the unique element of having to worry about Wisecrack below 30% HP.   FEALTY CAN BLOCK WISECRACK.  INVINCIBLE + FANATIC'S DRINK CAN THEN BE USED TO RIDE THINGS OUT UNTIL CHARM WEARS OR PEOPLE WHO DIDN'T GET CHARMED KILL THE NM.  Chaos roll + Ageha are probably even more important than normal since you can't use food.

Promathia Route T2: Bismarck

It's possible to tear through him with melees.  But, magic damage is probably more effective in a pick up group because for some reason pick up players don't like using food.

It's relatively foolproof to use a Botulus Rex style strategy for this. 2-3 COR, 3-4 BLMs, an Ochain PLD + WHM to hold the adds off to the side, and random melees + BRD/BLU/NIN to proc.  Wildfire + BLMs are an effective way to deal with this NM, since he doesn't take reduced magic damage (I don't think he even has much Magic Defense Bonus, if any), and he has high defense.  I also suspect he has low INT.

Bismarck has astoundingly low damage output.  Even during long periods without Fanatics, people rarely died.  Attacks seem to randomly have additional effects (Terror happened at one point) and will randomly attack people with its tail.  But, fanatics!  Gains shock spikes occasionally, which cannot be dispelled.  Casts Water + Thunder magic, but nothing destructive.  It moves pretty slow for a VWNM (No enhanced movement speed).

PLD should be first voke on the NM so the adds pop on the PLD.

Thar She Blows is instant death.  Just don't get hit by it.  It's not blocked by fanatics, and some people will die to this, but you should be fine.

Also, remember for all these fights, Ageha + Chaos roll are your friends.

Attowha Chasm: Fjalar + Bloody Skull (up to 3)

This is the hardest.  He likes to do everything he can to prolong the fight.  He spawns Bloody Skulls after Hellsnap (AoE Stun) and they cast spells including gaIII and Sleepga.  This is problematic.  Fjalar also likes to AoE Terror/Damage (Thundris Shriek).  His unique moves are Dunur Strike (low AoE Damage) and Bilfrost Squall (high AoE Damage).   Cackle inflicts several status effects, most importantly Magic Defense Down.  It MUST be removed.

Strategy:  PLD is not required for this NM.  Although there may be working strategies with a PLD on the main NM and DDs killing skulls.  I had success as follows:

1.) Ride fools drink, not fanatics drink.  Scherzo helps with your ability to do this.

2.) Weaken the NM and buff up as much as possible.  Ageha + Dia II(I) + Chaos Roll and damage will go much faster.  Only use Bio II+ if it's necessary.

3.) Form a clerics drink order to remove Cackle.  TP moves will destroy you with MDEF down up, but won't kill you otherwise for the most part.

4.) Ignore the adds completely, except maybe to TP on after Thundris Shriek (which imparts an intimidation effect).

5.) Just like any other VWNM, if it stays proc'd, it can't hurt you.  There's obviously a bit of a luck element in that!

Actually, according to Wowwiki (lol):

Proc is a common term used primarily in game programming to refer to an event - a "procedure" - triggered under particular circumstances. For example, in WoW, a particular weapon (that hits many times) might have a 10% chance on each hit to apply a special effect, such as poison damage. When WoW users talk about "how often this weapon procs", they are talking about the likelihood of the special effect occurring.

Proc was originally short for "spec_proc" (spec_proc is short for "special procedure") which is a term used by the original programmer of Circle-MUD, Jeremy Elson. It might have been used as well by the original programmers of diku-MUD as well. Special procedures in Circle-MUD are functions that can be assigned to objects, players, and locations in the world such that each time an event occurs, the special procedure function will be invoked. Special procedures were used in Circle-MUD for a wide variety of purposes: Creating room events when a person typed a specific string of text, causing a weapon or piece of armor to perform a magical action, and even causing a MOB (mobile) to do something that it wouldn't normally do.

When developers and players were talking about these special procedures they abbreviated the term to "proc". Over time the noun also became a verb, "proced" ("proc'd" or "procced"), which meant that the special procedure was invoked and performed its action.

"Programmed Random OCcurence" is another definition, thought to be correct by many WoW users, though whether or not it is indeed correct is debatable.

A standard pet-supertanking Voidwatch setup works for Morta.  The Rafflesia pop several seconds after she spawns, so you'll want to either have the PLD pop or voke it off of whatever unfortunate mage you made do the popping because no one else had the abyssite.  Once the adds spawn, the PLD can hatelessly supertank them off to the side ( dedicated WHM support recommended) while the rest of the alliance takes Morta away.  Her TP moves, spells, and damage potential is actually quite low, but she has pretty high evasion, defense, and her high level means that level correction is going to slow down your melees in general.  Chaos roll is recommended for both melee parties, and Ageha really helps too.

PLD/WAR WHM/SCH BLM/something BLM/DRK RDM/BLM BLU/DRG | NIN/DNC COR WHM/SCH WAR/SAM* SAM/WAR* MNK/WAR* | COR DRK/WAR* SAM/WAR* WAR/SAM* BRD/WHM WHM/SCH is my usual target setup for Morta.  RDM/BLM is the dedicated stun.

Of course, other setups work too, this is just what I generally bring.

Her Greek counterpart is Atropos, which lends its name to the plant genus containing Atropa belladona, deadly nightshade, as well as atropine, the toxic compound derived from it ("Atropine Spore"). Belladonna (italian for "pretty lady" - also hinted at in "Beautiful Death") is indeed one of the common names for deadly nightshade, and lends itself to Morta's family name (Belladonna sap) and synthesis material drop.

Acicular Brand and Orogenesis are physical TP moves while Crystallite Shower, Phason Beam, Crystallite Shower, Graviton Crux, Crystal Bolide and Fragor Maximus are magic (but still affected by Fanatic's Drink of course).

Crystallite Shower does Dia+Slow+Addle.

Graviton Crux absorbs HP and one random attribute from each player.

Crystal Bolide does Obliviscence+Terror, Terror Screen should be used under 50%.

Fragor Maximus does Weakness and gives Provenance Watcher a strong intimidation effect. Proccing with magic/Stun becomes difficult.

Damage from his melee attacks depend on which side you are. Tail is aoe 900-1200 dmg, claw does 600-900 dmg (single target or aoe with add stun) and Head is aoe 250-300 magic dmg (if you're in front of Provenance Watcher)

PLD RDM BRD SMN NIN BLU

COR WHM WAR DRK SAM MNK

SCH COR(RNG) BLM BLM BLM BLM

Adjustment content

B) The gameplay is shit, but relative to most other games, still decent. However, everything is currently a zergfest. If the event doesn't rely on 2-hour abilities, which encourage a zerg-style approach to combat due to the low duration and high recast of these abilities, then it requires something like overpowering temporary items. It comes down to members in the group being sufficient to deal enough damage with their main mode of death-dealing to kill the target(s) in the time it takes for those 2-hours to wear off, or those temporary items to become more sparse. Zerg zerg zerg zerg zerg.

C) The loot fest isn't fun. A major contributing factor to this is B, the content isn't fun to begin with, however the loot itself isn't fun. Outside of juggernauts like Nyzul gear, you don't have a fuckton to look forward to with each gear upgrade.

D) Horrible customer service/fan appreciation. Fuck Square-Enix. They're a bad company, they do not listen to the consumer on issues that matter. They've always been bad at running an MMO, but it's getting worse as time goes by.

My opinions anyway, though I know they're shared by some, if not many. Shit's critical, it isn't difficult to see.
